# A window's menu whose entries an `if` adds after the first frame: picking
# Save runs its handler, which the window's title reads, on every target.
#
# The bar's `if menu.length() > 0` cannot be settled, so html built the bar as
# an instance at run time, and lifting it made each value the menu's records
# read a prop of their own -- `saved` with them -- so Save's handler wrote the
# instance's copy and the pick ran nothing anyone saw, with no error
# (liftValues now carries such a handler whole). The condition counts the
# same records, handlers and all, and the walk translating the platform's
# intrinsics never entered a condition, so their `UpdateComponent` for the
# title reached JavaScript raw. And on bubbletea, which draws no menu, the pick
# calls the handler read off the list the branch builds, and NoTernary hoisted
# no ternary out of a callee.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component app root {
    var deep = false
    var saved = 0

    ui.window #main(title="Saves {saved}") {
        component menu {
            if deep {
                ui.menuItem(label="File") {
                    ui.menuItem(label="Save", @select { saved += 1 })
                }
            }
        }
        ui.button #dive(text="dive", @click { deep = true })
    }
}

func testAPickInAMenuShownLaterRuns(t test.Test, c app) {
    c.dive.click()
    c.main.menu[0].select()
    c.main.menu[0].children[0].select()
    t.assert(c.saved == 1)
    t.assert(c.main.title == "Saves 1")
}

app()
